answer.rationale: Competitor price cut directly targeting SMB base creates immediate churn risk. Memory_73 confirms targeted promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive SMB segments with strong acquisition and revenue lift. This is the only candidate action explicitly validated for this exact segment and threat vector. However, promotional pricing carries downstream risk: it may commoditize perception, train price sensitivity, or erode positioning. Small guarded test (time-limited, cohort-scoped offer to at-risk accounts) allows us to defend the SMB base while preserving option value. If churn stabilizes, we can then layer in memory_31 (signup simplification) and memory_86 (onboarding shortening) to improve activation durability and reduce future price sensitivity through faster time-to-value. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well for *retention* of established customers, not acquisition defense. Activation messaging (memory_91) and enterprise sales assist (memory_44) do not address the immediate competitive threat to SMB. A small test also preserves our ability to pivot if the competitor escalates further, without committing full margin erosion across the entire SMB cohort.
